name: Eggshell Green
lede: Eggshell Green is a pale, soft green, recorded by Maerz and Paul with a first-use date of about 1824.

sections.title: A pale green, dated early
sections.body:
Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary, by the account the NBS carried into its 1955 circular, puts the name's first printed record at about 1824, on plate 27 H 3 [1]. The ISCC-NBS system reads the swatch as a light green, about 7.3 units from the block center, a looser match than most names in our library [1].

The nearest named color in our data is [[niagara-green]], about 5.1 units off, with [[cambridge-blue]], [[cameo-green]] and [[deep-glaucous-green]] close behind [2]. The hue sits closer to blue-green than to the yellow-green of grass.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: This color, as photographed, appears in 55 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.23 percent, rarer than 59 percent of the named colors we track [3]. It peaks in the 1800s, in 10 of 8,345 paintings, at 0.1 percent of that period's paintings, 1.0 times the overall rate [3]. Inside a painting it most often plays a light [3]. The earliest match in the archive is a 1480 painting by Bernardino Jacobi Butinone, 450 years before the name's 1930 record, so this is a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not a pigment identification, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3].

issues: Fixed: the field-notes paragraph (and the matching "field" object) invented a movement claim ("over-represented in Mughal painting") with no basis — ar.mv is empty for this slug — and a peak-decade stat (1870s/0.5%/4x) that doesn't match the real century fact (1800s/0.1%/1.0x). The presence count (30) also didn't match either real count (25 within-painting / 55 as-photographed). Rewrote the paragraph directly from data/graph/fieldnotes for this slug; removed every unsupported claim rather than inventing a replacement for it.
